title: Magnolia Health onprem scaling constraints and Terraform sparse-state notes
body:
Purpose
This document captures a draft playbook for Magnolia Health's on-prem/private deployment: sizing constraints, Terraform sparse-state approach, upgrade plan, and operator runbook. Focus is on predictable latency for chat endpoints, safe TF state handling across air-gapped segments, and a pragmatic cutover strategy for a phased rollout.

Context & constraints (Magnolia-specific)
- Primary workloads: interactive charting assistant and policy-document summarization; 95th pct target latency 250ms for short-context chat (<=512 tokens).
- Data residency: full patient PII must remain on-premise, control plane in customer's VPC with restricted egress.
- Network: leaf/spine with 25Gbps NICs on inference nodes; MTU still 1500 in existing DC (can't change for now).
- Ops: internal IT controls change windows (Mon/Wed 02:00-06:00 local) and requires an audible runbook for any infra changes.
- Maintenance: nightly backups allowed only to a customer-managed NFS behind the same VPC.

Sizing assumptions (ballpark, for planning only)
- QPS pattern: baseline 40 p95 QPS across endpoints, peak 140 QPS during business hours.
- Typical request size: mean prompt 150 tokens, response 70 tokens.
- Target token-per-second throughput per GPU (estimated): 500 tokens/s for A10G 24GB under q4_0 quantized variant; 3500 tokens/s for H100 80GB FP16.
- Suggested node types for initial phase (cost/latency trade-off):
  - Inference pool A (latency-focused): 6 x H100-80GB GPUs, each in pods serving low-latency chat routes (pinning + KV cache). Expected peak capacity ~ 6 x 3500 = ~21k tokens/s.
  - Inference pool B (cost/backfill): 8 x A10G-24GB GPUs for batching high-throughput summarization. Expected peak capacity ~ 8 x 500 = ~4k tokens/s.
  - Control & orchestration: 3x m6i-large control-plane VMs for model manager, metrics, and telemetry.
- Storage: KV cache store sized at 1.2TB per H100 rack (estimate for 12M active prefixes), on NVMe-backed nodes.

Operational sizing table (illustrative)
- Small phase (MVP): 2 H100s + 4 A10Gs, 2 NVMe cache nodes (1TB usable), expected headroom ~30% for baseline traffic.
- Medium phase: 6 H100s + 8 A10Gs, 3 NVMe cache nodes (3TB usable), target for sustained ~140 QPS peaks.
- High-availability target: duplicate inference clusters across two racks with active/active routing and graceful fallback to a cheaper region.

Terraform sparse-state approach (why we propose it)
- Magnolia requested minimal GitOps footprint inside their restricted environment. Full remote backend (S3) is disallowed for sensitive TF state except behind the customer VPC.
- Proposal: use a sparse-state pattern where each logical component manages its own TF workspace/state file (control-plane.tfstate, inference-pool-1.tfstate, networking.tfstate, kms.tfstate). This limits blast radius when iterating and allows targeted, time-bounded locks for maintenance.

Key TF module notes and recommendations
- Module layout suggestions (module names are recommended names only):
  - network/vpc: creates subnets, route-tables, and peering. Variables: allowed_cidrs, control_plane_subnet_ids, mtus. Output: transit_gateway_attachments (string).
  - infra/baremetal-instances: provisions VM definitions + GPU attach wiring. Variables: instance_type, gpu_count, nvme_size_gb, hostnames_prefix.
  - serving/runtime-config: configmaps, model-versions, rollout-policies. Variables: default_batch_size, kv_cache_size, kernel_profile.
  - security/kms: wraps customer KMS/HSM integration. Use provider aliasing for customer KMS API.
  - storage/nfs: mounts, export ACLs, backup hooks.

Sparse-state operational notes:
- Use local backend for initial bootstrapping on customer jumpbox. Immediately after provisioning, copy state files into a customer-managed secure blobstore (not public S3). Keep a mirrored copy in an encrypted archive (customer policy).
- Locking: use a lightweight lock service (consul or etcd) inside customer VPC. If not available, adopt manual advisory locks via ticket-driven change windows.
- tfstate migration: include documented migration steps (scripted) to merge state files into a single remote backend when customer policy allows.

Upgrade and cutover plan (phased)
- Phase 0: Preflight (1–2 weeks)
  - Confirm network MTU, confirm SR-IOV support on NICs, collect GPU firmware versions.
  - Run a HW compatibility script (provided) to validate drivers and PCIe layout.
  - Create baseline TF workspaces in a staging account on customer's jumpbox.
- Phase 1: MVP deploy (night window)
  - Deploy control-plane + 2 H100 + 2 A10G with minimal models. Smoke tests: token-generation latency under 350ms for short prompts.
  - Validate KV cache persistence across restarts.
- Phase 2: Scaling and soak (2–4 weeks)
  - Add remaining inference nodes. Enable autoscaling knobs but keep conservative max limits.
  - Run synthetic RL/TV load tests that mimic peak QPS, measure p95 latency and cost curves.
- Phase 3: Canary upgrade and traffic migration
  - Canary 10% traffic to new pool for 48h. Monitor quality regressions (use eval prompts set). If regression >2% on eval pass-rate, rollback automatically to previous model version.
  - Full cutover only after 7 days of stable canary.
- Emergency rollback: keep previous model variant pinned in control plane and an automated pipeline that can re-route traffic within 5 minutes.

Q&A (internal notes and unresolved questions to raise with Magnolia)
- Q: Are sustained GPU host counts allowed to be >10 per rack (power + cooling)? A: Need DC confirmation; assume initial 10/GPU per rack hard limit until confirmed.
- Q: Does Magnolia have an internal lock service (consul/etcd)? A: IT said no in initial survey — follow up required. This impacts tfstate locking strategy.
- Q: Is KMS backed by a networked HSM or only customer-managed IAM keys? A: Pending. If HSM exists, integrate with security/kms module; otherwise use envelope encryption pattern.

Terraform snippets and examples (illustrative)
- Example workspace bootstrap (local jumpbox):
  - terraform init -backend-config=path=control-plane.tfstate ./control-plane
  - terraform apply -var "instance_count=3"
- Example variable set for serving/runtime-config module:
  - default_batch_size = 4
  - kv_cache_size = "1200GB"
  - kernel_profile = "h100-8x"

Runbook & operator checklist (day-to-day)
- Daily health checks (automated): GPU temperature, GPU util %, KV cache hit ratio, model load errors, 95th pct latency dashboard.
- Pre-change checklist (must pass before applying TF changes): backups of relevant tfstate files, maintenance window ticket open, rollback steps documented with OS-level snapshots, notify Magnolia IT 1h before window.
- Incident quick actions:
  - If p95 latency > 500ms: scale up KV cache nodes first, then add GPU pods to latency pool.
  - If nodes OOM on quantized models: force-model-fallback to less aggressive quantized variant or to CPU-based offline batch mode for that route.

Risks & mitigations
- Risk: tfstate divergence across sparse files when resources cross-module reference. Mitigation: keep cross-resource references minimal; use outputs to pass only stable identifiers (subnet IDs, kms IDs) and avoid creating the same resource in two modules.
- Risk: network MTU and NIC driver mismatch causing packet drops at 25Gbps. Mitigation: conservative throughput testing and MTU rollback plan.
- Risk: Slow KV cache warmup after restarts. Mitigation: persistent NVMe-backed cache and staged restart where only one pod restarts at a time.

Open action items
- Asha: follow up with Magnolia infra team to confirm HSM/KMS details (due 2025-03-05).
- Daniel: produce the HW compatibility script and attach to Confluence (PR #89).
- Ops: create a drill/runbook play for tfstate lock failure scenarios and share during next on-call rotation.

Appendix: quick checklist for TF sparse-state migration script
- Step 1: export individual tfstate files and validate resource IDs do not overlap.
- Step 2: run terraform state rm on duplicate references and re-import into consolidated workspace using terraform import.
- Step 3: run terraform plan in a read-only dry-run and have customer sign-off.

Notes: this is intentionally prescriptive but still a draft. Magnolia-specific constraints drove the sparse-state recommendation; if they relax remote backend policies we should prefer a single encrypted remote backend for easier lifecycle management.

-- end of draft --
